solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Wriggle, as maiden taken by nobleman endlessly (6)

indicators.note: the maiden is led off by the nobleman, so she walks behind him and her letter comes after his
without its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: SQUIRE, a country gentleman, loses its last letter
M = maiden, a cricket scoring abbreviation

annotation.surface: A young woman squirms as a lord leads her off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taken by' puts the maiden after the nobleman. A maiden is an over with no runs in cricket, marked M on the scorecard.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs describe twisting the body about, and squirm adds the embarrassment the maiden might feel.

entries.clue: Something that goes with status rocker once mentioned (6)

blocks.note: a Teddy boy, a 1950s rock'n'roll fan

annotation.surface: An old rocker cited as part of the establishment.
annotation.walkthrough: Teds were British 1950s youths in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock'n'roll, hence 'rocker once'. 'Status' is not a position here but the first half of a Latin phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of cited: a figure quoted in a report is one mentioned there.

entries.clue: International regrets about revolutionary soldier in plots (9)

indicators.note: turning over, so the soldier is written backwards
the regrets go round the soldier

annotation.surface: Remorse at an international level over a rebel fighter caught up in conspiracies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary soldier' suggests a guerrilla, but it only means the GI turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both plural nouns for secret schemes against someone, as in court intrigues.

entries.clue: Brilliant burner gives a nasty singe for mother to cover up (9)

indicators.note: the letters of SINGE are messed up
to cover something up is to put a layer over it on all sides, so MUM surrounds the other letters

annotation.surface: A fierce flame singes someone, and mother has to hide the damage.
annotation.walkthrough: The burner is not a stove or a fire but a metal that burns with a dazzling white light.
annotation.definitionFit: Magnesium burns with an intensely bright white flame, used in flares and old camera flashes.

entries.clue: Crystalline material found by fellow falling over in pit (8)

indicators.note: toppling, so MALE is written backwards
the fellow falls in the pit, so his letters end up within MINE

annotation.surface: A miner who tumbles into a shaft discovers a crystal seam.
annotation.walkthrough: Melamine is best known as a hard plastic for tableware, but the compound itself is crystalline.
annotation.definitionFit: Melamine is a white crystalline compound used to make resins.

entries.clue: Instrument making no sound needs to get fixed inside (7)

indicators.note: the repair is done on the inside of the instrument, so SET sits within the letters of MUTE

blocks.note: to set = to become fixed, as glue or jelly does

annotation.surface: A silent instrument needs repair work inside.
annotation.walkthrough: An instrument 'making no sound' sounds like a broken one, but it just gives MUTE.
annotation.definitionFit: A musette is a small bagpipe, popular in 17th- and 18th-century France.

entries.clue: Manchester United could obviously lose – reverse starts with substitute (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word
then read those letters backwards

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

annotation.surface: A football pundit says Manchester United may lose, so bring on a substitute.
annotation.walkthrough: The football picture makes 'substitute' look like a player coming off the bench; it is a stand-in doctor or cleric.
annotation.definitionFit: A locum is someone standing in temporarily for a doctor or priest.

entries.clue: Bread dull, so we hear (5)

indicators.note: what follows is by sound, not spelling

annotation.surface: Someone reports that the bread is boring.
annotation.walkthrough: Matt is the British spelling of matte, a non-shiny finish.
annotation.definitionFit: Matzo is the unleavened bread eaten at Passover.

entries.clue: Rude teen must be disciplined, altered (8)

indicators.note: the letters are knocked into a new order

annotation.surface: A cheeky adolescent must be punished and changed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Altered' is the euphemism for a neutered pet, which gives the surface a darker second reading.
annotation.definitionFit: A euphemism: vets and pet owners say altered for an animal that has been sterilised.

entries.clue: Small houses can be prisons with excessive staying in (8)

indicators.note: to stay in is to remain indoors, so the excess keeps inside the prisons

annotation.surface: A gloomy remark that a tiny home can feel like a jail if you're stuck in too long.
annotation.walkthrough: OTT (over the top) is common British shorthand for excessive.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the word names a modest dwelling, typically rural, so small houses is its plain gloss.

entries.clue: Fruit – it comes with mostly hard outer covering (6)

indicators.note: IT arrives wrapped in the covering
all but the last letter of CRUST

annotation.surface: A description of fruit with a tough rind.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'hard outer covering' fits the fruit's own peel, which is the disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: Citrus fruit covers oranges, lemons, limes and their kin.

entries.clue: Catty female totally heartless having row (6)

indicators.note: the whole middle goes, leaving only the ends

blocks.note: FEMALE with all of EMAL removed

annotation.surface: A spiteful woman, completely cold, picking a quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts you to read a quarrel, matching catty; it is a line. Heartless usually drops one middle letter; 'totally' removes all four.
annotation.definitionFit: Feline means cat-like, which is what catty literally means.

entries.clue: Book / a singer (3,5)

blocks.note: Henry Fielding's 1749 comic novel about a foundling
the Welsh pop singer of 'It's Not Unusual'

annotation.walkthrough: The slash just divides the two definitions.
annotation.definitionFit: Tom Jones is Henry Fielding's 1749 novel and also the Welsh pop singer.

entries.clue: A bit is missing from supporting beam (3)

indicators.note: the letters IS are removed

blocks.note: a joist is a floor beam; take IS out of its middle to leave JO and T

annotation.surface: A piece of a supporting beam has gone missing.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'is' in 'is missing' is also the letters to remove: the clue uses the word twice over.
annotation.definitionFit: A jot is a tiny amount, as in 'not a jot'.

entries.clue: Country with marriage and civil partnership, say? (6,6)

definitions.text: Country with marriage and civil partnership, say?

blocks.note: the surface wants a nation's laws; the answer is a nation's name

blocks.clueFragment: with marriage and civil partnership, say?
blocks.note: each is a state of being joined, a united state, and two of them make the plural

annotation.surface: A question about a nation that recognises both marriage and civil unions.
annotation.walkthrough: Marriage and civil partnership are both states of being united, so the country is literally 'united states'.
annotation.definitionFit: The United States is the country, and each union is a united state.

entries.clue: Character in inferior position, it seems (9)

annotation.surface: Someone with personality stuck in a lowly post.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It seems' flags that the answer read as SUB STANCE is only a joke on the word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of solid worth: a person of substance has real character.

entries.clue: A famous swimmer grabbing kiss from great man (9)

indicators.note: the swimmer takes the kiss inside

blocks.note: Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to see Hero
X = a kiss at the end of a letter

annotation.surface: A celebrity swimmer snatching a kiss from a VIP.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great man' is not praise but a title: Alexander the Great.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Macedonian conqueror carries 'the Great' as his title, so the clue borrows his epithet.

entries.clue: Part of road giving entrance for traffic into naval base (4,4)

indicators.note: the first letter, the way in
the traffic drives into the base, so its T goes inside FASLANE

blocks.note: Faslane, the Royal Navy submarine base in Scotland

annotation.surface: Directions for traffic entering a navy base by road.
annotation.walkthrough: Faslane on the Clyde is the home of Britain's nuclear submarines.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the overtaking lane of a motorway is one strip of the carriageway, so part of a road.

entries.clue: Maybe dean’s gloomy journey in the churchyard? (5,7)

indicators.note: the letters of DEANS could be otherwise arranged

annotation.surface: A clergyman's sombre walk among the graves.
annotation.walkthrough: The dance of death was a medieval image of skeletons leading the living to the grave, so the 'journey' ends in the churchyard.
annotation.definitionFit: A danse macabre is an allegorical procession of the dead, which suits a trip through a churchyard.

entries.clue: The reverse of eager, mostly I’m alarmed! (3)

indicators.note: KEEN loses its last letter
read what remains backwards

annotation.surface: Far from keen, someone yelps in fright.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is an exclamation, so it swaps for a cry of fright.
annotation.definitionFit: An interjection defined by the feeling behind it: the squeak of fright stands for a whole exclaimed sentence.

entries.clue: Plant vehicle somewhere away from home (7)

blocks.note: away = not at home, as in an away match

annotation.surface: An instruction to leave your car somewhere far from home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb, to park a car; it is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Caraway is a plant grown for its aromatic seeds.

entries.clue: See bird wag diving under water (6)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the wag goes below the water

blocks.note: a wag is a joker, a wit

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher points out a bird whose tail dips into the water.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wag' looks like a tail movement; it is a joker. To pass water is to urinate, hence PEE.
annotation.definitionFit: The peewit is the lapwing, named for its call.

entries.clue: Martinet, persistent type giving learner detention (8)

indicators.note: the sticker holds the learner in

annotation.surface: A strict teacher keeps giving a pupil detention.
annotation.walkthrough: The school scene makes 'detention' a punishment; it just means holding L inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict disciplinarian, a stickler for rules.

entries.clue: Where land meets sea / take it easy (5)

blocks.note: the verb for moving along without effort, as a bike freewheels downhill

annotation.walkthrough: The slash divides the two definitions, a noun and a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: The coast is the shoreline; to coast is to proceed with little effort.

entries.clue: Coffee after appointed hour – little time for drinking (5)

indicators.note: LATE drinks in, so swallows, the T

annotation.surface: A late coffee, with barely time to drink it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'For drinking' looks like it belongs with the coffee; it is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with steamed milk.

entries.clue: Bullet in drawer (6)

blocks.note: a round that burns as it flies, leaving a visible trail
one who draws by tracing over an image

annotation.surface: A gun kept in a desk drawer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is one who draws, not furniture.
annotation.definitionFit: A tracer is a bullet that leaves a visible trail, and also someone who traces drawings.

entries.clue: Scholar with old Bible in South Africa? Not all the Bible (6)

indicators.note: the Bible is located in South Africa, so AV sits within SA

blocks.note: the Authorised Version, the 1611 King James Bible
the New Testament, only part of it

annotation.surface: A learned man in South Africa with an antique Bible, but not the complete text.
annotation.walkthrough: The Bible is used twice: once as AV, the whole old translation, and once as NT, only one half of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French, where savant means knowing; both name someone of deep learning.

entries.clue: Storm over? Chill out (4,4)

blocks.note: a storm is a strong wind
down = over, finished, as in a wind that has died down

annotation.surface: Once the storm has passed, time to relax.
annotation.walkthrough: The weather picture makes 'chill' sound cold; it means relax.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: both phrasal verbs mean to unwind and relax after a busy spell.

entries.clue: The early worms – tough (8)

indicators.note: the letters wriggle into a new order

annotation.surface: The early bird's worms turn out chewy.
annotation.walkthrough: The proverb 'the early bird catches the worm' makes 'worms' look like a noun; it is a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: like leather, something leathery is hard to chew or cut, the sense of tough meat.

entries.clue: Time to admit bad person’s mistakes (6)

indicators.note: to admit is also to let in, as a ticket admits you, so ERA takes RAT inside

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

annotation.surface: It is time for a rogue to own up to his errors.
annotation.walkthrough: The ’s is short for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Errata are listed errors in a printed work.
